newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to form task force to sever racketeer links.
newsitem.headline: Japan to form task force to sever racketeer links.

text.p: Japanese cabinet ministers will form a task force next week to consider what can be done to help break ties between companies and racketeers, ministers said on Friday.
"We must keep close contact and come up with an effective package to deal with corporate racketeers," Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a regular news conference.

Racketeers, or so-called "sokaiya", often linked to "yakuza" crime syndicates, typically try to extort money from firms by threatening to expose dubious business practices in their publications or by raising embarrassing questions at shareholders' meetings.

Many former senior officials of Nomura Securities Co Ltd and Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd have been arrested for allegedly making payoffs and also making loans without appropriate collateral to a sokaiya.
The ministers' task force, involving major ministries, will be formally launched on July 15, Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama told a news conference.
Japan's justice, finance, police and trade ministries will form the core of the task force, which will hammer out concrete proposals.

They will work to prepare a legal framework to impose stricter penalties on firms with links to corporate racketeers and strengthen inspection of financial firms and policing over racketeers, Kajiyama said.
The core group will also ask business groups to cut ties with racketeers, he said.
Both Nomura and DKB said on Thursday they will cancel subscriptions to periodicals, many of which financial experts say are really tools for extortion.
Kyodo news agency reported on Friday that 13 major Japanese banks submitted a written oath to the metropolitan police that they will cut ties with corporate racketeers.
